newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom cost belies takeover rumors.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom cost belies takeover rumors.

text.p: WorldCom Inc stock and options continued in huge trading activity Monday on persisent bid rumors, but analysts said the cost of buying the company and likely earnings dilution for any buyer made a bid unlikely.
"With the acquired debt and a premium you would be talking about a takeover approaching $30 billion," said Richard Klugman of brokers PaineWebber.

WorldCom stock was up 7/8 up at 23 at 1100 EST/1600 GMT on volume of 3.3 million shares. Volumes last week were as high as 11 million shares per day, five times the stock's usual volume, and January expiring calls were very active.
"It would probably be dilutive to anyone who bought it," said Mark Kastan of brokers Merrill Lynch.
Klugman said, "GTE has been mentioned a lot and that has kept the options bubbling."

GTE Corp's own market capitalization is around $44 billion. GTE has always declined comment on rumors about WorldCom but told analysts it had been in very broad talks with many companies in recent months.
WorldCom's takeover of MFS Communications Co Inc was approved by shareholders on Friday. The deal is expected to be dilutive to earnings for three years.
The combined company has debt of $3-$4 billion, analysts say.
Nevertheless, analysts were at a loss to explain quite why WorldCom options activity was so great, particularly as the stock price had moved sideways to lower in recent sessions.

Some of the options in greatest demand were at an exercise price well above the current share price -- making them of no intrinsic value -- and would expire within a month. If there is no bid, then a lot of people will lose a lot of money.

Analysts noted that WorldCom escaped the recent raft of bad news that hit other second-tier long-distance companies such as Frontier Corp and LCI International Inc, so there may be some flight to quality by investors.

Frontier told analysts earlier this month that fourth quarter earnings would be below those of a year ago, while LCI told analysts that while it would report earnings and revenue growth for the quarter, future revenue growth rates would be scaled back to 30 percent a year from 40 percent.
